fixes.explanation: Carmel doesn't show up in this passage, friend. Moses names two mountains for the proclaiming: the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal. Keep Gerizim for the blessing and Ebal for the curse, and you've got the pair.

A lamb every morning isn't on Moses' list here. What he names is fearing the LORD by walking in all His ways, loving Him, serving Him with all the heart and soul, and keeping His commandments and statutes. No lamb anywhere in it. Keep the lamb out of this one, baker.

Close to something you might expect, but that isn't the word here. Moses says the commandments and statutes are given for Israel's own good. Testing isn't mentioned in this verse. Think of the timer on my oven: it's there to help the batch, not to catch anybody.

Moses says the opposite, friend. He says the LORD set His affection on Israel's fathers and loved them, and that He has chosen Israel, those fathers' descendants, “…above all the peoples, even to this day.” So the answer here is true. That's a lot of love to read past.

That's right, friend. Moses says the LORD “…executes justice for the fatherless and widow…” Leaving them to fend for themselves isn't what he describes. He says it right after telling Israel the LORD shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
Yes, baker. Moses says the LORD “…loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.” Food and clothing are two things anybody can use. And the very next verse tells Israel to love the foreigner too.

That's it, baker. Moses says, “So you also must love the foreigner, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.” That's the reason he gives them. I think anyone who's been the new person in a room knows what he's getting at.

Not quite, friend. Moses says their fathers went down to Egypt, seventy in all, and now the LORD has made Israel “…as numerous as the stars in the sky.” So Israel isn't that small today. Seventy is where they started, and the stars are the comparison Moses picks.
Moses doesn't mention a plague here, baker. He says the earth opened its mouth and swallowed Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab the Reubenite. This is a heavy part.

Moses says more than that, friend. The earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram, “…their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.” So the households and tents went too. I think this line hurts, and I think Moses wanted the people to take it seriously.

That's right, baker. Moses says the earth opened its mouth and swallowed Dathan and Abiram, “…their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.” So it wasn't just the two men. This is a heavy part.

Yes, baker. Moses says keeping every commandment is “…so that you may have the strength to go in and possess the land…” Israel is about to cross the Jordan, and strength is what he names for going in. Strength is exactly what you want before a big move.

Wells don't appear in this verse, baker. Moses says the land drinks in the rain from heaven. It's a land of mountains and valleys, and that's different from Egypt, where they irrigated on foot (Deuteronomy 11:10).

Water from a rock isn't in this promise, friend. For the livestock, the promise says, “…I will provide grass in the fields for your livestock…” It comes right after the promise of rain in season. The grass is the answer.

Shelter isn't what's promised here, baker. For the livestock, the promise says, “…I will provide grass in the fields for your livestock…” Valleys do show up earlier in the passage, but not for this. It's grass for the animals.
Shake isn't the word, friend. Moses says the LORD “…will shut the heavens so that there will be no rain…” It comes with the warning that the land won't yield its produce. This is a heavy part.

Moses says something much bigger, friend. He wants the words spoken about “…when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.” No altar or feast day is named in that verse. Those are everyday moments at home and on the road.

Once a year wouldn't match what Moses says, baker. He says to speak about these words “…when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.” That's sitting, walking, lying down and getting up, not one date on the calendar. Repeat a recipe that often and you'd never forget it.

Yes, baker. Moses says it's a blessing if they obey, "…but a curse if you disobey the commandments of the LORD your God and turn aside from the path I command you today…" Two roads, and Moses sets both in front of them that day.

That's it, baker. Moses says to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal. He also says where they are: across the Jordan, near the Oak of Moreh. Gerizim is the mountain for the blessing.
